Laura / Priyom —

Looping you both in to confirm current behavior and to propose an operational workflow for FintechCo's asks. Quick summary of what Maria requested:
- PT backups: default retention and purge cadence
- Per-customer snapshot preservation (on-request)
- Whether application & audit logs that include PII follow the same purge rules or have separate longer retention options

CloudTriage (our backup subprocessor) can confirm topology; Priyom, can you confirm cost/ops for extended snapshot preservation and the request ticket SLA? Laura, can you weigh in on whether we can offer a 14-day "canary restore window" (preserve recent snapshots for 14 days outside of the standard purge) and a separate log-exception process (30/90-day ad-hoc preservations) under an addendum to the DPA?

Attached: request to CloudTriage for a current S3 snapshot map (ask them to attach), and internal deletion_runbook_v1.2 to reference the deletion workflow.

Proposed workflow (high-level):
1) Customer requests extension via support ticket (HubSpot HS-98765).
2) Security approves exception (email approval from customer's security contact + Redwood sec owner).
3) Ops creates a preserved snapshot and flags it in metadata; snapshot marked for separate purge timeline.
4) If DPA erasure requested, we follow deletion runbook steps: application tombstone -> metadata scrub -> backup dereference + certificate of destruction for preserved snapshots.

Notes: backups are managed by CloudTriage in us-east-1 by default; we'll need their confirmation on the 'dereference' mechanics (can they zero-out individual customer objects or do we need to expire a whole snapshot?). CloudTriage, please reply with the exact purge cadence and options.

-David

Hi David / team —

Summary for FintechCo:
- Subprocessor: CloudTriage (backup & snapshot management) — primary region us-east-1; secondary replication in us-west-2 for DR.
- Standard retention: incremental point-in-time backups are retained for 30 days by default. Full snapshots are retained for 90 days.
- Per-customer preserved snapshots: available on request. We create a preserved snapshot and tag it; preserved snapshots can be held for up to 180 days at our standard preservation rate (we've quoted similar for other customers). Preservation requires a written request from the customer's security contact and a signed addendum if >90 days.
- Log retention: application logs that include PII are stored in a separate logging cluster. Default retention is 30 days. We can extend log retention to 90 days on request; 180 days requires an approved addendum and a scoped agreement (we do not recommend >180 for PII).

On deletion mechanics: we can "dereference" objects for a single customer by removing object pointers and zeroing out object contents for specific keys, but full immutability guarantees depend on the underlying object store lifecycle and replication. For preserved snapshots we maintain metadata flags and can provide a certificate of deletion when we purge the preserved snapshot. For full DPA erasure workflows, we recommend the sequence David outlined: application tombstone -> metadata purge -> backup dereference -> preserved-snapshot purge + certificate.

Attached: s3_backup_map.csv (stub) that shows account buckets and replication regions.

Let us know if you need us to draft the DPA addendum language for extended retention/preservation and we can provide a scoped clause for 90/180-day exceptions.

—CloudTriage Support

Maria / Legal —

Thanks for the clear ask. To summarize and propose next steps from Redwood:
1) Default behavior: incremental backups — 30 days; full snapshots — 90 days; logs — 30 days.
2) Short-term investigation support: we can offer a 14-day canary restore window (preserve last 14 days of snapshots outside normal purge) at no additional cost for one-off investigations, provided we have written approval from FintechCo security and an internal Redwood sec-owner.
3) Extended preservation: we can preserve snapshots up to 180 days for customers via a paid addendum. CloudTriage will tag preserved snapshots and provide a certificate when they purge.
4) DPA erasure workflow: Redwood will follow the documented deletion_runbook_v1.2 sequence. For preserved snapshots that are in scope of erasure, we will coordinate dereference + zeroing with CloudTriage and issue a certificate of destruction.

Action items: 
- FintechCo Legal: please review the attached DPA addendum proposal (dpa_addendum_proposal.docx) that adds scoped exceptions for 90/180-day snapshot preservation and log-retention up to 90/180 days. If acceptable, sign and return; if you need edits, mark changes.
- David: please prepare the internal approver list and designate the Redwood sec-owner for this customer (I recommend David as owner; please confirm).
- Priyom: provide an Ops runbook checklist and cost estimate for >90 day preservation.

If we get the signed addendum we can update HubSpot HS-98765 and schedule the preservation within 48 hours.

—Laura
